headline: Margins expand on an adjusted basis as GAAP profit falls
summary_short: WTW's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 9% y/y to $2.47 billion (5% organic), but GAAP diluted EPS fell 27% to $2.43 on Newfront-related integration costs, while Adjusted Diluted EPS rose 17% to $3.35 as adjusted operating margin expanded 100bps to 19.5%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 9% y/y (5% organic) to $2.47B, led by Risk & Broking (+11%, 7% organic, on new business and client retention) and Health, Wealth & Career (+8%, 4% organic, on retirement and outsourcing work). GAAP diluted EPS fell 27% y/y to $2.43 on $61M of Newfront transaction/integration expense and higher interest expense; Adjusted Diluted EPS rose 17% to $3.35 as adjusted operating margin expanded 100bps to 19.5%. H1 free cash flow rose to $360M from $217M. Cash fell to $1.63B (-17% y/y) after $1.04B of Newfront cash outlay and $750M of buybacks; long-term debt rose 21% y/y to $5.78B. Board raised buyback authority by $1.5B. FY2026 guidance reaffirmed; Propel targets ~30% adjusted operating margin by 2028.

drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based: Risk & Broking revenue rose 11% (7% organic) on new business activity and strong client retention; Health, Wealth & Career rose 8% (4% organic) on retirement, outsourcing and communications project work.

GAAP diluted EPS fell mainly on $61M of Newfront-related transaction and integration expense (vs $2M a year earlier) and higher interest expense from acquisition financing; Adjusted Diluted EPS, which excludes these items, rose 17%.
Decline mirrors the EPS driver: higher transaction/integration costs and interest expense outweighed underlying segment operating income growth.
Fell y/y as $61M of Newfront transaction and integration expense and higher unallocated corporate costs offset 12% growth in segment operating income to $564M.
Cash fell mainly on $1.04B used for the Newfront acquisition and $750M of share repurchases in H1, partly offset by $474M of operating cash flow.
Rose y/y after $775M of new debt borrowing during the period, used in part to help fund the Newfront acquisition.

Management called results 'solid,' citing business momentum and disciplined execution, and announced Propel — a new AI/automation plan targeting ~30% adjusted operating margin by 2028 — alongside a $1.5B increase to share buyback authority.
